probes.support_reason: Deterministic tie-break answered YES for every numbered sub-requirement. F-1: (1) `Named` is an abstract type declaring one operation `tag` returning `[]const u8`, Zig's ordinary text-string type; (2) `A` and `B` are two distinct concrete types supplying `tag` implementations that return "a" and "b"; (3) `const items = [_]Named{ ... };` is a single sequence whose DECLARED element type is `Named`, holding one `A` value and one `B` value, and the concrete type of an element is NOT recoverable from `Named`, whose data field is `*const anyopaque`; (4) `return items[0].tag();` dispatches at runtime through the stored function pointer to `A`'s implementation and produces "a". F-2/F-4: core language only, no flag beyond the frozen recipe. F-3: builds under `zig build-exe -OReleaseSafe` and prints a. F-6: no normative prohibition; `anyopaque` and function pointers are documented first-class facilities. The canonical_task's NONE branch does not apply: Zig DOES have a type through which values of two different concrete types are held in one sequence with a common operation dispatched to the concrete implementation at runtime. It is not a built-in one -- Zig has no interface, trait or protocol construct -- so it is written by hand as a record of an erased data pointer and a function pointer, which is exactly the shape `std.mem.Allocator` and the 0.16 `std.Io` interfaces use. The absence of a language construct is charged in tokens (173, against Rust's 84 and Go's 73) and in complexity units, not in the support level. R10 record: selected form = 173 tokens. Alternatives considered: a `union(enum) { a: A, b: B }` element type would be far shorter but is rejected by R1, because sub-requirement (3) requires that the concrete type NOT be recoverable from the declared element type, and a tagged union's tag recovers it exactly; storing only the function pointer and dropping `ptr` would be shorter but is rejected by R1, because sub-requirement (3) requires the sequence to hold the `A` and `B` VALUES; `std.ArrayList(Named)` instead of an array literal is more tokens and the task asks only for a sequence.
